t:
(a) 
Notwithstanding any provision to the contrary in the governing instrument or under any law applicable to the District of Columbia (except as provided in subsection (e) of this section), the governing instrument of any corporation organized under the laws of the District of Columbia, or under any Act of Congress applicable to the District of Columbia, which is treated during a particular year as a private foundation described in section 509 of the Internal Revenue Code of 1954 shall be deemed during such particular year to contain the following provisions:

        (1) 
The corporation shall not engage in any act of self-dealing which is taxable under section 4941 of the Code.
 
        (2) 
The corporation shall make, distributions at such time and in such manner as not to subject it to tax under section 4942 of the Code.
 
        (3) 
The corporation shall not retain any excess business holdings which would subject it to tax under section 4943 of the Code.
 
        (4) 
The corporation shall not make any investments which would subject it to tax under section 4944 of the Code.
 
        (5) 
The corporation shall not make any taxable expenditures which would subject it to tax under section 4945 of the Code.
   With respect to any such corporation organized prior to January 1, 1970, subsection (a) shall apply to taxable years beginning on or after January 1, 1972.

    (b) 
The governing instrument of any corporation described in subsection (a) may be amended, in the manner provided by law for amendment of such governing instrument, expressly to include the provisions required by section 508 (e) of the Code.
 
    (c) 
The provisions of subsection (a) shall not apply to any corporation to the extent that its governing instrument is amended in the manner provided by law for amendment of such governing instrument, expressly to exclude the application of subsection (a).
 
    (d) For purposes of this section, the term “corporation” includes an association (other than an association treated as a trust described in section 1801 of title 21 of the District of Columbia Code).
 
    (e) 
For the purposes of this section, the term “Code” means the Internal Revenue Code of 1954.

fable.w: This section deems the governing instruments of District of Columbia private foundations to contain certain tax-related restrictions and lets those corporations amend their own instruments. The tempting reading is that the amendment provisions in subsections (b) and (c) give outside parties a role, but those are private corporations changing their own documents, not outsiders being consulted on a federal decision. There is no comment period, hearing, advisory body, consultation, rulemaking authority, or right to sue.
fable.s: The corporation shall not engage in any act of self-dealing which is taxable under section 4941 of the Code.

opus.w: This section makes certain tax-related provisions part of the governing instruments of D.C. private foundations by default, and it lets corporations amend their instruments to include or exclude those provisions. No federal decision-maker has to consult, hold hearings with, or take comments from anyone outside the government, and no one gets a right to challenge a federal decision. A corporation amending its own charter is private governance, not participation in a federal decision.
opus.b: Someone might read this as participation because private corporations can amend their own governing instruments to include or exclude these provisions. That reading doesn't hold up. Those amendments are private choices about a corporation's own charter. They are not consultation or coordination with the federal government before it makes a decision.

qwen_chat.w: This section imposes regulatory and tax compliance requirements on corporations treated as private foundations. It does not require the federal government to consult with, coordinate with, or seek advice from these outside entities before making a decision. The interaction is purely regulatory (compliance with tax code provisions), which falls outside the definition of participation that requires outside involvement in the decision-making process itself.
qwen_chat.s: The corporation shall not engage in any act of self-dealing which is taxable under section 4941 of the Code.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that because the section references "corporations" and "private foundations" (which are outside entities), and imposes rules on them, it involves participation. However, the definition explicitly states that "applications for benefits or grants" are not participation, and more broadly, regulatory compliance requirements imposed on outside entities without a mechanism for those entities to consult, coordinate, or advise the government before a decision is made do not constitute participation. This section merely deems certain provisions to be part of a corporation's governing instrument for tax purposes; it does not require the government to consult with these corporations or allow them to participate in the decision-making process regarding the law itself.
